scenarios: the provider fails the first three attempts whatever their profile: the generated variant and both repairs fail, the third repair is refused (at most 2), and the known-good fallback — the frozen protocol with 24 turns — runs and verifies; the experiment is shadow only, no baseline written
audit: NOT-FOUND: no profile variant existed to repair, and nothing consumed a trial's failure signals to change one.
proof: The real harness, CLI and Core with a staged scripted provider; each attempt in its own scratch workspace.
negative_proof: The third repair is refused; on Windows CI the fallback was first rejected by the gate because a shared scratch directory leaked a previous attempt's __pycache__ into the base — fixed by per-attempt scratch directories and byproduct exclusion, after which Windows verifies.
limitations: The failure is forced by the provider, so the test proves the bound and the fallback, not that a repair helps; repair maps two features, not the full failure taxonomy (REQ-EV-0245).

ci.note: all jobs green on macOS, Linux and Windows
